gloss: to drag on into; to carry over into (overtime, etc.)

definitions.gloss: to drag on into; to end up extending into (overtime, a later stage)
definitions.explanation: For a contest, negotiation, or dispute to fail to be settled and spill over into an additional stage such as extra time, a playoff, or a further round. Combines もつれる (to become tangled/deadlocked) with {込|こ}む (to move into).

examples.japanese: {試合|しあい}が{延長|えんちょう}にもつれ{込|こ}む。
examples.english: The game drags on into extra time.

examples.japanese: {交渉|こうしょう}は{最終日|さいしゅうび}までもつれ{込|こ}んだ。
examples.english: The negotiations dragged on all the way to the final day.

examples.japanese: {両者|りょうしゃ}{譲|ゆず}らず、{勝負|しょうぶ}はサドンデスにもつれ{込|こ}んだ。
examples.english: Neither side would give way, and the contest went into sudden death.

notes:
An intransitive verb. The thing that drags on takes に to mark what it extends into (extra innings, a playoff, a final day, etc.).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {延長|えんちょう}にもつれ{込|こ}む: to go into overtime/extra innings
- {最終|さいしゅう}{戦|せん}にもつれ{込|こ}む: to come down to the final match
- {混戦|こんせん}にもつれ{込|こ}む: to develop into a close, tangled contest

USAGE:
Most often used of sports, elections, and negotiations that stay unresolved and spill into an extra stage. Implies the outcome was hard-fought and undecided.
